blocks.content: The Finance Commission is envisaged as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.

rows: Devolution of central taxes and grants-in-aid
Quasi-judicial powers to summon records and witnesses
Constituted every 5th year by the President

items: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are purely advisory in nature and not legally binding on the Union Government.
Qualifications of the Chairman and members are not specified in Article 280 itself, but in the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 enacted by Parliament.
The Finance Commission has all the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 while summoning documents and evidence.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 280 to ensure non-partisan allocation of financial resources.
Members are appointed by the President of India, but their qualifications and selection process are determined by Parliament through the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
The Commission possesses quasi-judicial powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, allowing it to summon witnesses and require production of public records.
Recommendations made by the Commission are advisory in nature, though established conventions mandate serious consideration by the Central Government.
It acts as the principal balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India by determining tax devolution and grants-in-aid to States.
